title: Can I Take Another Dose? DoseBench: Evaluating LLM Decision-Making in OTC Dosing QA
abstract: arXiv:2606.04262v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to answer everyday health questions online, including whether someone can take another dose of an over-the-counter (OTC) medication. Yet this common safety-relevant setting remains underexplored in medical QA. Answering these questions requires checking previous doses, timing, and product-specific dosing limits, while recognizing when important information is missing. We introduce DoseBench, a focused benchmark of 230 consumer-style acetaminophen and ibuprofen dosing questions with human-annotated YES, NO, and AMBIGUOUS labels, and evaluate eight LLMs with five responses per question. Overall accuracy ranges from 44.8% to 62.2%, while models incorrectly approve 14.0% to 60.5% of prohibited doses. Models with similar accuracy can therefore make very different dosing decisions. Additional analyses show that these failures are not easily fixed by giving models more guidance. Askin

translated_title: 我能再吃一剂吗？DoseBench：评估大语言模型在非处方药剂量问答中的决策能力
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于在线回答日常健康问题，包括某人是否可以再服用一剂非处方（OTC）药物。然而，这一常见且与安全相关的场景在医学问答领域仍未得到充分探索。回答这些问题需要核对之前的用药剂量、用药时间以及特定产品的剂量限制，同时还要识别何时缺少重要信息。我们提出了DoseBench，这是一个包含230个消费者风格的对乙酰氨基酚和布洛芬剂量问题的专用基准，每个问题均带有“是”、“否”和“不明确”的人工标注标签，并评估了八个大语言模型（每个问题获取五个回答）。总体准确率介于44.8%至62.2%之间，而模型错误批准的禁用剂量比例高达14.0%至60.5%。因此，准确率相近的模型可能会做出截然不同的用药决策。进一步的分析表明，这些错误无法通过向模型提供更多指导而轻易修复。
tldr: 该论文提出了DoseBench基准，通过230个人工标注的非处方药剂量问答评估八个大语言模型，发现其决策准确率仅44.8%至62.2%，且会错误批准大量禁用剂量，凸显了LLM在用药安全场景中的重大风险。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DoseBench, a benchmark of 230 human-annotated OTC dosing questions showing that LLMs achieve only 44.8%-62.2% accuracy and frequently approve prohibited doses, revealing serious safety risks in medication-related QA.
